findings.title: Webhook settles inline before answering; Moyasar requires a quick 2xx before complex logic
findings.evidence: webhook(): after payment_event_record the handler runs `await settlePayment(deps, paymentId.toLowerCase(), event.live, event.id)` (fetchPayment + fetchInvoice, each with a 10 s timeout, then apply_verified_payment) and only then `return accepted()`. Moyasar's webhook reference: 'Your endpoint must quickly return a successful status code (2xx) before any complex logic that could cause a timeout.' (https://docs.moyasar.com/docs/api/other/webhooks/webhook-reference.md). The delivery timeout is undocumented (contract item 9).
findings.impact: Under a slow provider the reply can take 20+ s; if Moyasar's delivery timeout is shorter it marks the delivery failed, retries 5 times (each answered duplicate -> 200) and its dashboard shows failed webhooks. Money is safe (the event is durable before the settle; the job finishes it), but the vendor's stated requirement is not met and the owner sees spurious webhook failures.
findings.proposed_fix: Answer 200 right after payment_event_record (state recorded) and run settlePayment detached (EdgeRuntime.waitUntil when available, else let the job pick the event up at its next_check_at = now()+30 s), or measure the delivery timeout in E02 run 1 before deciding.

findings.title: Invoice-callback throttle is keyed on the caller's IP, i.e. on Moyasar's egress address: it caps the provider, not an abuser
findings.evidence: callback() passes `p_ip_hash: await clientKeyHash(request, pepper)`; payment_callback_begin (supabase/migrations/20261002100000_payment_core.sql:1343) does `rate_limit_take('payment-callback:ip', p_ip_hash, 60, interval '1 hour')` and answers `{}` silently when over. Every genuine callback comes from Moyasar's few egress IPs (cf-connecting-ip on hosted), so all paid invoices of an hour share one bucket of 60.
findings.impact: After 60 paid invoices in an hour the callback does nothing for the rest of the hour; settlement then depends on the webhook, the return page and the job (no money lost), and the throttle gives no protection against a forger, who comes from other addresses anyway.
findings.proposed_fix: Key the callback throttle on the invoice id hash (one fetch per attempt per 5 s is already enforced by fetched_at) or raise the per-IP cap well above the expected sales rate; keep the 5-second fetched_at rule as the real guard.

findings.title: Runbook still says the emulator accepts a past expired_at; the emulator refuses it with 400 since the sandbox alignment
findings.evidence: Runbook: 'An invoice that has `expired_at` in the past at creation is accepted and is `expired` at once.' Emulator createInvoice() lines 664-667: `else if (typeof expiredAt === 'string' && Date.parse(expiredAt) < Date.now()) { errors.expired_at = [...] }` -> 400 validation_error; tests/unit/moyasar-emulator.test.ts:467 says the API refuses a past expiry 'as the sandbox does'. Runbook line 87 in the same file already states the 400.
findings.impact: A developer writing a test or a probe from the 'harness choices' list expects an immediately expired invoice and gets a 400; the file contradicts itself.
findings.proposed_fix: Delete the bullet at line 155 (or reword: a past expired_at is refused 400, as the sandbox answered).

findings.title: Contract section 9 describes the emulator's cancel reply and error bodies as they were before the sandbox alignment
findings.evidence: Contract: 'PUT /v1/invoices/:id/cancel (... a `canceled` one answers 200 again ...)' and line 467: '400 {type:'invalid_request_error', message:'Validation Failed', ...}'. Emulator cancelInvoice() lines 711-720 answers 400 `refusedOperation('Cancel failed. The Invoice is already canceled.')` for a canceled invoice, and invalid() line 245 answers `{type:'validation_error', message:'Data validation failed'}`; moyasar-sandbox-2026-10-02.md 'What this changes' records the alignment, but section 9 was not updated.
findings.impact: The plan of record misdescribes the harness later rounds and E02 scripts are written from; a brief written from section 9 would assert a 200 that the emulator (and the sandbox) answer 400.
findings.proposed_fix: Update section 9: a canceled or expired invoice answers 400 invalid_request_error 'Cancel failed. The Invoice is already …'; a refused field answers 400 validation_error 'Data validation failed' with an errors map; a past expired_at is 400.

findings.title: Contract and runbook state a documentation conflict about invoice metadata that the vendor has since closed
findings.evidence: Contract: 'The API reference's create-invoice request schema omits `metadata`; the guide and the metadata page include it. A documentation conflict, to confirm in the sandbox.' (repeated at docs/payments-runbook.md:41). Today https://docs.moyasar.com/api/invoices/01-create-invoice lists `metadata` (object) in the request body: 'A set of key-value pairs where both key and value are strings.' The sandbox also confirmed it on 2026-10-02.
findings.impact: None on the code; the record says a conflict is open that no longer exists. The vendor now says values are strings while the sandbox kept a numeric value: the client's string-only filter (moyasar.ts:276) remains right.
findings.proposed_fix: Mark the row resolved (the reference documents metadata as of 2026-10-06) in both files.

findings.title: Emulator is stricter than the sandbox on metadata: refuses non-string values and answers {} instead of null when none was sent
findings.evidence: metadataProblem(): `if (typeof item !== 'string' || item.length > 500) return 'values must be strings...'` -> 400; createInvoice() line 688 stores `{}` when no metadata was sent. The sandbox record (moyasar-sandbox-2026-10-02.md item 1): 'An invoice made without metadata answers `metadata: null`. A numeric metadata value is kept as a number.' The client reads `metadata: z.record(...).nullish()` and keeps string values only (moyasar.ts:243, 276), so both shapes are handled.
findings.impact: Nothing hidden today (the code sends two string values and handles null). A future test that relies on the emulator refusing a numeric value, or on `{}`, would pass locally and differ live.
findings.proposed_fix: Store null when no metadata was sent and accept numeric values (kept as numbers) to match the sandbox; or list the two differences under the runbook's 'harness choices'.

findings.title: Emulator caps a refund of a captured payment at `amount`; Moyasar caps it at `captured`
findings.evidence: refundPayment(): `if (payment.refunded + amount > payment.amount) return invalid(...)` for paid, captured and refunded alike. Vendor: 'For `captured` payments, the maximum refundable amount is the `captured` amount.' (https://docs.moyasar.com/docs/guides/payment-operations/index.md). A `captured` payment only ever reaches the ledger as a review payment (apply_verified_payment UNEXPECTED_STATUS) whose amount_halalas is the payment's `amount`, and refund_request bounds EXCEEDS_BALANCE by that amount.
findings.impact: A refund of a partially captured review payment for more than `captured` passes the ledger and the emulator but would be refused 400 live (refund -> failed REFUND_REFUSED, nothing moved): safe, but the emulator cannot show it. Hosted invoices are not expected to produce captured payments.
findings.proposed_fix: In the emulator bound a captured payment's refunds by `captured`; optionally store `captured` on review payments and bound EXCEEDS_BALANCE by it.

findings.title: payments_kick gives pg_net 15 s while a reconciliation run may legitimately last 60 s plus one row; whether the function survives the disconnect is unproven
findings.evidence: `perform net.http_post(..., timeout_milliseconds := 15000)` with the comment '15 s: a cold function start can exceed pg_net's 5 s default.' runPaymentsReconcile (payments.ts:48, 680) takes rows for up to RUN_BUDGET_MS = 60_000 and the row in progress may add a cancel, an invoice fetch and one fetch per charged payment at 10 s each. pg_net gives up at 15 s on every run longer than that.
findings.impact: If the Edge runtime stops the handler when its client disconnects, every run longer than 15 s under a slow provider ends without job_run_record (the last recorded run reads ok) and the rows keep only their 2-minute lease; if it does not, pg_net merely logs timeouts. Either way the comment's reasoning covers the cold start only, not the run's own length.
findings.proposed_fix: Prove it once (recipe); then either raise timeout_milliseconds above the run budget (e.g. 90000) or shorten RUN_BUDGET_MS to fit under it.
findings.proof_recipe: Local stack with the emulator: set Vault functions_url/jobs_secret; `POST /__emulator/fault {route:'GET /v1/invoices/:id', mode:'timeout', times:3}`; make one pending attempt due (`update finance.payment_attempts set next_check_at = now() where id = $1`); `select public.payments_kick()`; after 90 s: `select status, detail, started_at from finance.job_runs where job = 'payments_reconcile' order by started_at desc limit 1` and `select timed_out, status_code from net._http_response order by created desc limit 1`. Wrong result: no job_runs row for the run (handler killed at the 15 s disconnect) while _http_response shows timed_out = true.
findings.prior_overlap: R3-L4 (the 60 s budget) added the budget without revisiting the kick timeout

findings.title: A webhook refused for a wrong secret leaves no trace anywhere the owner can see
findings.evidence: `if (!secretsMatch(event.secret_token, deps.config.webhookSecret)) return failWith(401, ...)` before any write, and the module 'Nothing here logs'. A secret mistyped in the dashboard (or pasted with a trailing newline, since secretsMatch is exact) makes every delivery 401; Moyasar retries 5 times and drops it (webhook-reference.md). Orders still settle through the callback, the return page and the job, so the admin shows nothing wrong.
findings.impact: A misconfigured webhook secret is invisible except in Moyasar's dashboard; the system silently runs on the slower prompts (callback capped per EF-MONEY-02, job backoff up to 30 min), and the first symptom is a late receipt. Not a money risk.
findings.proposed_fix: One `console.warn('payments: webhook refused UNAUTHORIZED')` (no body, no token) so the hosted function logs show it, and a runbook line under step 2 telling the operator to check the Moyasar webhook log after the first payment.

findings.title: Turnstile siteverify is called without idempotency_key, so a 5 s timeout spends the buyer's single-use token
findings.evidence: verifyTurnstile posts `{secret, response, remoteip}` with `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5_000)` and no retry; a timeout answers UNREACHABLE (503 TURNSTILE_UNAVAILABLE at checkout.ts:437). Cloudflare: 'each token can only be validated once' and `idempotency_key` (UUID) exists 'for safely retrying validation requests' (https://developers.cloudflare.com/turnstile/get-started/server-side-validation/). When siteverify consumed the token but the reply was lost, the buyer's retry with the same token answers timeout-or-duplicate -> INVALID_TOKEN -> 400 'تعذّر التحقق من أنك إنسان.'
findings.impact: After a transient siteverify stall the buyer is told they failed the human check and must redo the widget; the order is not created either way (fail closed), so the cost is a confusing message and a lost checkout under Cloudflare slowness.
findings.proposed_fix: Send `idempotency_key: crypto.randomUUID()` with the request and retry the same body once on UNREACHABLE; or map a timeout-or-duplicate that follows a timeout to TURNSTILE_UNAVAILABLE so the form re-renders the widget instead of blaming the visitor.
findings.prior_overlap: EF-comms-3 (AUDIT-2) covered operator-side codes, not the spent-token case

findings.title: The return page's verify answers an order's payment state to anyone who knows its 8-character number (no token)
findings.evidence: verify(): `const tokenHash = accessToken ? await orderAccessTokenHash(pepper, accessToken) : ZERO_HASH` then payment_check_begin; finance.payment_view (payment_core.sql:581-595) computes `state` from the order alone and gates only `invoiceUrl` on the token. Throttle 120/h per IP hash. The contract (section 6, payment_check_begin) specifies this so the return page works when the tab lost its stored order.
findings.impact: Anyone holding an order number (it is in the success_url query, on the receipt, in support mail) learns whether that order is paid, pending, expired, cancelled, refunded or under review. No money or personal data; a deliberate design trade-off, recorded so it is not rediscovered.
findings.proposed_fix: None required; if tightened later, answer `unknown` without a token except for the states the return page must show (pending, paid), keeping the token-less path for the tab that lost its token.
